references.text: Describes the daily burnt offering that was to be brought morning and evening, which forms the basis for the sacrificial system detailed in Numbers 28
Refers to 'a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ), the same expression used in Numbers 28:2
Calls the offering 'the Lord's food' (לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה), corresponding to the phrase 'my bread' (לַחְמִי) in Numbers 28:2
Uses the expression 'their God's bread' (לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיהֶם) regarding the offerings, parallel to 'my bread' in Numbers 28:2
Introduces the chapter on the Lord's appointed feasts (מוֹעֲדֵי יְהוָה), the same theme as 'at its appointed time' (בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ) in Numbers 28:2
Refers to a fire offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, using the same language as in Numbers 28:2
Prophesies about the daily burnt offering in the future temple, a continuation of the system from Numbers 28
Describes Christ's offering as 'a gift and an offering, a pleasing aroma to God' (εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας), fulfilling the Old Testament sacrificial system of 'pleasing aroma'
